| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 1. **Standalone**         | `sched-ui serve --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080`            | a UI next to a daemon in one command |
| 2. **Embedded at a path** | host `dist/` statically under `/sched`, `?api=/sched/api` | mount the UI inside your app         |
| 3. **Components**         | `<sched-runs base="/api" token="…">` in your page         | build the UI into your own markup    |
| 4. **Custom UI**          | `createAdminApi` from `@schedjs/admin-api`                | your own panel, CLI, or client       |

## 1. Standalone

```bash
npm i -g @schedjs/ui        # or: npx @schedjs/ui
sched-ui serve --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080 --port 8081
```

Open &#x2A;*<http://127.0.0.1:8081>{rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}**. `/api/*` is proxied to the daemon on the same
origin — no CORS setup, and the Bearer token never leaves the browser→sched-ui hop.

> **Cache control.** The bundle (`/sched-ui.bundle.js`) is served with
> `Cache-Control: no-store` and `/api/*` proxy responses with `no-cache` — a
> rebuilt UI or a fresh run snapshot is never served stale from the browser cache.

## 2. Embedded at a path

Host the built `dist/` of `@schedjs/ui` under any path (nginx, CDN, your app's static
folder) and point it at your admin api mount:

- `dist/index.html` is the shell — open `https://you.example/sched/`
- query overrides: `?api=…`, `?token=…`, `?refresh=…` (e.g. `?api=/sched/api`)

## 3. Components

```html
<script type="module" src="/sched-ui.bundle.js"></script>
<sched-runs base="/api" token="…" limit="50"></sched-runs>
<sched-tasks base="/api"></sched-tasks>
<sched-schedules base="/api"></sched-schedules>
```

Components are Lit custom elements — they work in any framework. Theming is via CSS
custom properties (`--sched-bg`, `--sched-card`, `--sched-line`, `--sched-text`,
`--sched-muted`, `--sched-ok`, `--sched-bad`, `--sched-run`): override them in your
own stylesheet to match your brand.

Run deletion in `<sched-runs>` is two-step: the row's **del** button arms to &#x2A;*sure?**
and only a second click within 3s deletes (auto-disarms on timeout or refresh) — a
stray click can't wipe a run.

**Auto-refresh** — every list (`<sched-runs>`, `<sched-tasks>`, `<sched-schedules>`)
polls the admin api on the `refreshMs` interval (property, or the `refresh-ms`
attribute; default 5000 ms) so live fields — run status/progress, next-run and
last-run times, fail counts — stay current; set `refreshMs=0` to disable polling.
The shell sets this from the `?refresh=…` query override.

**Last status** — `<sched-schedules>` and `<sched-tasks>` show a `last status`
column (✔ succeeded / ✘ failed / ⊘ cancelled) so you can see how the most recent
run ended at a glance. The value comes from the server (`lastRunStatus` in
`GET /schedules` / `GET /tasks`), resolved in one pass — the browser does not
fetch the run per row.

**Schedules are first-class** (schedule-as-entity) — `<sched-schedules>` lists each
schedule row: `task`, rule, `tz&#x60;, &#x2A;*`data`** (the per-tenant parameters), next run,
last run + status, and the **effective pause status**: 🔴 `paused (task)` when the
family stop holds the schedule, 🟡 `paused (schedule)` when only this instance is
paused, ▶ `active`. The two levels are shown separately so «снял паузу, а оно
молчит» never happens — `resume` on a schedule held by the task still shows 🔴
until `resume` is called on the task.

**Runtime rows** — a schedule whose task is runtime-only (`fileManaged=false`, e.g.
created via the API, not `tasks.json`) shows a `runtime` badge next to the task name.
File-managed rows (from `tasks.json`) have no badge.

**Manage schedules** — the `+ new` button opens a form (task picker from `GET /tasks`, kind cron/interval/once + value, tz, data JSON, externalId, dedupKey,
retry JSON, priority); it POSTs `/schedules` (a `dedupKey` makes the second save an
upsert, not a duplicate). Each row has **pause / resume**, **edit** (`PATCH /schedules/:id` — the rule/tz/data/policy change in place, `nextRunAt` recomputes
on a rule change) and **delete** with a confirm (runs are kept — the audit
survives).

**Pagination** — every list (`<sched-runs>`, `<sched-tasks>`, `<sched-schedules>`) has a
footer: `‹ prev` / page-size select (10/25/50/100) / row range / `next ›`. Lists are
fetched with `limit + 1` rows to detect whether a next page exists (the probe row is
trimmed), so **next** is disabled on the last page and **prev** on the first. Changing
the page size resets to the first page. Page size defaults to 50 (set the `limit`
attribute); the current page offset is the `offset` attribute — set both to start the
list elsewhere.

## 4. Custom UI

`createAdminApi` exposes the same REST surface the components use — health, runs,
tasks, schedules, plus trigger / pause / resume / delete. See [Admin API](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/admin-api).

## Auth (SCHED\_ADMIN\_KEY)

With a key set on the daemon, the shell prompts for it in the header (saved to
localStorage) — or pass `?token=…` on the URL, or set `el.token` on components.

## Embedded apps (no daemon)

An embedded engine can mount the admin api itself and use any UI mode:

```ts
import { createEngine, createInternalRunner, createSqliteStorage } from '@schedjs/core';
import { createAdminApi } from '@schedjs/admin-api';

const engine = createEngine({ /* … */ });
const admin = createAdminApi({ engine, storage, auth: { apiKey: '…' } });

// in your http server, mount /sched/api → admin.handleRequest(req, res)
```

Then point the shell at it with `?api=/sched/api` (mode 2), or drop components into
your page (mode 3).


# MCP server

`@schedjs/mcp` exposes sched's control plane as a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.org){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} server.
An AI client (Claude Desktop, codex, pi, Cursor) can inspect and drive a running daemon — list tasks, read
run history, trigger runs, pause/resume — from natural language, with the same guarantees as the admin API.

The MCP server is a **projection of the admin API**: it never opens storage itself, it calls the daemon's
REST API with the same bearer key. The daemon stays the single owner of state.

> Docs MCP (search over these docs) is a separate, built-in server: Docus serves `/mcp` on the docs site
> (list-pages + read-page). This page is about the **product** MCP for managing sched.

## Install

```text
yarn workspace @schedjs/mcp build
```

## Run (stdio)

Default transport for local AI clients:

```text
sched-mcp --admin-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --api-key <SCHED_ADMIN_KEY>
```

Point your client at `npx sched-mcp` (or the built `dist/cli.js`) with the same arguments.

## Run (Streamable HTTP)

For remote/daemon-side hosting:

```text
sched-mcp --http 8091 --admin-url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --api-key <SCHED_ADMIN_KEY>
```

The HTTP mode is **session-based** (stateful Streamable HTTP): each client gets its own MCP
session — a `Mcp-Session-Id` header is issued on `initialize` and must be echoed on later
requests. Sessions are removed when the client sends `DELETE`, and are garbage-collected
after 30 min of inactivity, so a long-running server neither leaks transports nor clashes
on a shared connection. Unknown session ids are rejected with `404`.

## Options

| Flag              | Env               | Default                 | Meaning                                          |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `--admin-url URL` | `SCHED_ADMIN_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` | Admin API base URL                               |
| `--api-key KEY`   | `SCHED_ADMIN_KEY` | —                       | Admin API bearer key (open in dev mode if unset) |
| `--http PORT`     | —                 | stdio                   | Serve Streamable HTTP on PORT                    |
| `--readonly`      | —                 | off                     | Reject mutations; only list/get tools respond    |

## Tools

| Tool              | Args                           | Description                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_tasks`      | —                              | All tasks: name, runner, schedule, paused, next run                                                     |
| `get_task`        | `name`                         | One task, full config                                                                                   |
| `list_schedules`  | —                              | Schedules: taskName, schedule (cron/interval/once), tz, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, paused, effectiveStatus   |
| `get_schedule`    | `scheduleId`                   | One schedule: rule, tz, data, effectiveStatus                                                           |
| `create_schedule` | `taskName schedule tz?`        | Create (or upsert by `dedupKey`) a schedule (mutation); `data` validated against the task `inputSchema` |
| `update_schedule` | `scheduleId schedule? tz?`     | Edit a schedule in place (mutation, partial merge)                                                      |
| `pause_schedule`  | `scheduleId`                   | Pause one schedule instance (mutation)                                                                  |
| `resume_schedule` | `scheduleId`                   | Resume a paused schedule (mutation)                                                                     |
| `delete_schedule` | `scheduleId`                   | Delete a schedule; runs keep history (mutation)                                                         |
| `list_runs`       | `task? status? limit? offset?` | Runs, newest first; filter by task/status                                                               |
| `get_run`         | `runId`                        | One run: status, error, log, result, artifacts                                                          |
| `trigger_task`    | `name data?`                   | Run a task immediately (mutation); `data` validated against the task `inputSchema`                      |
| `cancel_run`      | `runId`                        | Cancel a running/queued run (mutation); a terminal run → 409                                            |
| `retry_run`       | `runId triggeredBy?`           | Re-execute a finished run with its original data (mutation)                                             |
| `pause_task`      | `name`                         | Stop scheduling a task (mutation)                                                                       |
| `resume_task`     | `name`                         | Resume a paused task (mutation)                                                                         |
| `delete_task`     | `name`                         | Delete a task; runs keep history (mutation)                                                             |
| `delete_run`      | `runId`                        | Delete a run from history (mutation)                                                                    |

Mutations (`trigger_task`, `pause_task`, `resume_task`, `delete_run`, `cancel_run`, `retry_run`, `delete_task`, `create_schedule`, `update_schedule`, `pause_schedule`, `resume_schedule`, `delete_schedule`) are disabled in `--readonly` mode.

## Safety model

- **Server-side validation** — schedules/statuses are validated by the admin API; unknown tasks/runs
  return a clear error, never a crash.
- **Read-only mode** — hard gate for automation: mutations answer with an explicit error.
- **Human approval** — the MCP server does not invent a confirm protocol; the confirm gate lives in
  the AI-client layer: the AI proposes, a human approves, the AI calls the mutation tool.


# CLI & daemon

Two binaries, one product:

| Binary   | Package           | Role                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schedd` | `@schedjs/daemon` | the process server (SQLite + tasks.json + runners + engine + optional admin api)                                      |
| `sched`  | `@schedjs/cli`    | the operator CLI — a thin client of the admin api (status/runs/tasks/schedules/trigger/pause/resume) + `check-worker` |

The daemon's binary was renamed `sched` → `schedd` (docker/dockerd precedent) so
the operator CLI could take the `sched` name. A global install of both packages
no longer collides.

---

# Daemon — `schedd`

A single process: SQLite storage + tasks.json desired state + per-task runners +
engine loops + optional admin server.

> **Node 24 requirement.** `schedd` requires Node >= 24 (`engines`): `node:sqlite`
> is stable there, so the one-line `ExperimentalWarning: SQLite …` that Node 22
> printed on every start is gone.

## Usage

```bash
schedd [--tasks tasks.json] [--db sched.db] [--lock-ttl SECONDS]
       [--lock-heartbeat SECONDS] [--retention-ttl SECONDS] [--temporary-retention-ttl SECONDS]
       [--poll-timeout SECONDS] [--tick-interval MS] [--watchdog-interval MS]
       [--admin-port PORT] [--admin-host HOST] [--storage SPECIFIER]
```

| Flag                        | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--tasks`                   | `tasks.json`   | Path to the desired-state file                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--db`                      | `sched.db`     | SQLite database path — &#x2A;*only valid with `--storage sqlite`** (XOR: a non-sqlite storage with an explicit `--db` fails fast)                                                                                    |
| `--storage`                 | `sqlite`       | Exactly **one** storage (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--lock-ttl`                | 1800 (30 min)  | Zombie-lock threshold in seconds                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--lock-heartbeat`          | 600 (10 min)   | Lock refresh cadence for long sync runs, seconds — &#x2A;*must be `< lock-ttl` (enforced at parse; the engine throws too)** (default: `lock-ttl / 3`)                                                                |
| `--retention-ttl`           | 2592000 (30 d) | Retention TTL for regular terminal runs, seconds from `finishedAt&#x60;. **`0` = retention off** — terminal runs are kept forever (archive semantics, see [Retention](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/#retention)) |
| `--temporary-retention-ttl` | 86400 (24 h)   | Retention TTL for `temporary&#x60; runs. **`0` = retention off for the temporary class**                                                                                                                             |
| `--poll-timeout`            | 1500 (25 min)  | Async (accepted) run ceiling in seconds — must be `< lock-ttl`                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--tick-interval`           | 1000           | Tick cadence in ms (due-task scan)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--watchdog-interval`       | 60000          | Watchdog cadence in ms (zombie reaping)                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--admin-port`              | —              | Serve the admin API (`/api/*`) on this port                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--admin-host`              | `127.0.0.1`    | Bind host for the admin server                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Environment

| Env var                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SCHED_ADMIN_KEY`         | Bearer key for the admin API/UI. Unset → API open (bind private host!). With a key set, the web UI accepts it via the **admin key** field in the header (saved to localStorage) or `?token=…` on the shell URL           |
| `DOCKER_HOST`             | Override the docker CLI context (used by the docker runner)                                                                                                                                                              |
| `MONGO_URL` (+`MONGO_DB`) | Connection string for `--storage mongo`. `MONGO_DB` overrides the db name from the URI path                                                                                                                              |
| `MONGO_RETRY_MS`          | Startup-connect retry budget for `--storage mongo` (default 30000). The initial connect is retried every 500 ms up to this budget before the daemon fails — a brief mongo restart does not crash-loop the daemon at boot |
| `MYSQL_URL`               | Connection string for `--storage mysql`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `PG_URL`                  | Connection string for `--storage postgres`                                                                                                                                                                               |

> **Connection strings live in env / config-volume only — never in arguments.**
> A connstring passed as a flag would leak into the process list (`ps`, `docker inspect`). The startup banner prints the kind + db name only
> (`storage=mongo db=<name>`), never the URL or credentials.

## Storage selection (`--storage`)

The daemon supports exactly **one** storage per process — the `--storage`
specifier (XOR with `--db`, which is the sqlite knob):

| Specifier                    | Storage                     | How it's wired                        |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `sqlite` (default)           | SQLite file (`--db`)        | built into `@schedjs/daemon`          |
| `mongo`                      | `@schedjs/storage-mongo`    | env `MONGO_URL` (+`MONGO_DB`)         |
| `mysql`                      | `@schedjs/storage-mysql`    | env `MYSQL_URL`                       |
| `postgres`                   | `@schedjs/storage-postgres` | env `PG_URL`                          |
| `<npm-package>` / `<./path>` | **custom** BYO module       | dynamic import → `createStorage(env)` |

Built-in kinds (`mongo|mysql|postgres`) resolve to their `@schedjs/storage-*`
package **at runtime** — the package must be present in the image, otherwise
startup fails fast:

```text
schedd: fatal: --storage mongo: add @schedjs/storage-mongo to your image (RUN yarn add @schedjs/storage-mongo)
```

A custom module must export `createStorage(env): Promise<Storage>` — the same
BYO contract as the built-in adapters ([Storage](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/storage)). `./`, `../`, `/`
prefixes resolve to a filesystem path (relative to the daemon's cwd); anything
else is an npm package.

```bash
MONGO_URL=mongodb://user:pass@db.internal:27017/sched schedd --tasks tasks.json --storage mongo
```

## Signals

| Signal                         | Behavior                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SIGINT` (Ctrl+C)              | Graceful stop — engine loops stop, sqlite closes, exit 0 |
| `SIGTERM`                      | Same graceful stop (POSIX; systemd, docker stop)         |
| `SIGBREAK` (Ctrl+Break, win32) | Same graceful stop — added for Windows operators         |

On Windows, `taskkill` sends a termination that does **not** always reach a
console process as `SIGTERM` — the reliable paths are Ctrl+C / Ctrl+Break.

## What the daemon does on start

1. Resolves the storage (`--storage`); a non-sqlite storage validates its
   connstring env **before** anything starts (missing env → fail-fast).
2. Syncs `tasks.json` into storage (desired state; removed tasks get disabled).
3. Validates every task's runner is registered — a missing runner **aborts startup**:
   `task "greet": runner "custom" not implemented in this build (registered: http, docker)`.
4. Starts the tick loop (fires due tasks), the watchdog (reaps zombie locks), the
   poll loop (async `accepted` runs), and the retention loop (hourly sweep of
   terminal runs past their TTL — `--retention-ttl` / `--temporary-retention-ttl`).

## Retention

Terminal runs (`succeeded` / `failed` / `cancelled`) are pruned by the retention
loop (hourly) once they're past their class TTL, measured from `finishedAt`:

- `temporary` runs → `--temporary-retention-ttl` (default **24 h**);
- regular runs → `--retention-ttl` (default **30 d**).

Set the TTL to **`0` to turn retention off for that class** — run history is kept
forever. This is the archive mode for deployments that migrate legacy history
into sched (books: migrated `task_runs` carry old `finishedAt` timestamps, and
with the 30 d default the first hourly pass would silently prune everything
older than a month — `--retention-ttl 0 --temporary-retention-ttl 0` keeps the
archive).

> Note: `0` was added in daemon 0.11.0. Earlier versions had no way to disable
> retention — a migration onto the 30 d default pruned aged history.

## Example

```bash
SCHED_ADMIN_KEY=dev-key schedd \
  --tasks tasks.json \
  --db sched.db \
  --admin-port 8080
```

Then the admin api answers on <http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/>{rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}\*. The operator CLI
(`sched status --admin-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/api`) and the web UI
(`npx @schedjs/ui` → `sched-ui serve --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080`, see
[Admin UI](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/ui)) both speak to it.

---

# Operator CLI — `sched`

`@schedjs/cli` — a thin projection of the admin REST API ([Admin API](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/admin-api)):
status, runs, tasks, schedules, trigger, pause/resume. Zero dependencies
(`node:fetch` only); the daemon stays the single owner of state. Machine output
is `--json`; tables are for TTY eyes only.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g @schedjs/cli
```

## Usage

```text
sched <command> [args] [--admin-url URL] [--api-key KEY] [--json]

Commands:
  status                   daemon health + task/schedule/run counts + next runs
  runs [--task T] [--status S] [--limit N] [--offset N]
  tasks
  schedules
  trigger <task> [--data JSON]
  pause <task> | pause --schedule <id>
  resume <task> | resume --schedule <id>
  check-worker <url> [--api-key KEY] [--timeout SECONDS]
```

Global flags:

| Flag                                | Env               | Default                     | Description                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--admin-url URL`                   | `SCHED_ADMIN_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/api` | Admin API base — note the `/api` mount point is already included |
| `--api-key KEY`                     | `SCHED_ADMIN_KEY` | —                           | Bearer key for the admin API                                     |
| `--json`                            | —                 | —                           | Stable machine-readable JSON contract                            |
| `-h` / `--help`, `-v` / `--version` | —                 | —                           | Help / version                                                   |

Exit codes: **0** ok / **1** api·network·data error / **2** usage.

`--api-key` before the command is the admin key; after `check-worker` it is the
*worker's* key (a different secret — see below).

## Examples

```bash
sched status                                   # is my daemon alive? next runs?
sched runs --status failed --limit 20 --json   # failed runs as JSON
sched trigger publish-video --data '{"videoId":"v-42"}'
sched pause --schedule channel-ada             # pause one channel's schedule, not the task
sched resume sync-channel-stats
```

`status` composes one view: `/health` + `/tasks` + `/schedules` + a bounded
failed-runs fetch, and lists the five soonest `nextRunAt` schedules.

## PowerShell note

Windows PowerShell 5.1 pipes UTF-16 by default — `ConvertFrom-Json` can garble
UTF-8 JSON from `sched --json`. Use `pwsh` (PS 7, native UTF-8) or `chcp 65001`
in cmd. Quote paths with spaces in examples.

## check-worker — conformance validator

Validates that an HTTP envelope worker ([Runner protocol](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/protocol)) speaks the
wire contract correctly — a fake-sched client that sends exactly the envelopes
sched sends and checks the answers. Never touches the daemon or the admin api.

```bash
sched check-worker http://127.0.0.1:8081 --api-key $SCHED_API_KEY --timeout 30
```

Six scenarios, each PASS/FAIL:

| # | Scenario           | Check                                                                                         |
| - | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | Sync success       | POST ping → 200 `{status:"succeeded"}`                                                        |
| 2 | Sync failure       | POST with `data.fail` → `{status:"failed", error}`                                            |
| 3 | Async lifecycle    | POST long → 202 accepted → GET statusUrl → running (progress grows) → succeeded, timeout trap |
| 4 | Auth               | only with `--api-key`: no key → non-2xx, with key → 2xx (skipped otherwise)                   |
| 5 | Run-id idempotency | two dispatches with the same run id → identical envelope                                      |
| 6 | Dirty input        | garbage body → worker answers 4xx/500 and stays alive (re-ping works)                         |

Verdict: `N/N PASS`, exit 0 all-green / 1 a scenario failed / 2 usage.
`--json` prints `{ ok, pass, fail, scenarios: [{name, pass, skipped, detail}] }`.

Worker contract for scenarios 1–5: `POST` with `content-type: application/json`,
`x-sched-run-id` (the idempotency key), optional `x-sched-api-key`, body
`{ task: { name, config }, data }` — exactly what the HTTP runner dispatches
(see [HTTP runner](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runners/http) and the examples in `examples/workers/`).


# Self-hosting

sched is self-hosted by design — a single daemon + SQLite, or the full Docker stack with
the web UI (shell).

## The daemon image

The official image is built from the **published** `@schedjs/daemon` npm package —
the artifact that passed the test/parity gates — not from monorepo sources:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
RUN echo '{"name":"schedd","private":true,"packageManager":"yarn@4.18.0"}' > package.json \
 && corepack enable \
 && printf 'nodeLinker: node-modules\nnpmMinimalAgeGate: 0\n' > .yarnrc.yml \
 && CI=1 yarn add @schedjs/daemon@0.10.2 \
 && yarn cache clean
ENV PATH="/app/node_modules/.bin:${PATH}"
ENTRYPOINT ["schedd"]
```

We publish `sched-daemon:<version>` to our registry
(`ghcr.io/schedjs`). Internal builds pull `@schedjs/daemon` from a private npm
registry: the token is passed as a **BuildKit secret** (never an
`ARG`/`ENV` — that would land in the image layers and `docker history`) and the
registry is pointed at it for the duration of the install only:

```bash
# private-registry build (public builds omit the secret + registry arg)
docker build \
  --secret id=registry_token,env=NPM_REGISTRY_TOKEN \
  --build-arg NPM_REGISTRY=https://registry.npmjs.org \
  -t ghcr.io/schedjs/sched-daemon:0.11.0 apps/daemon
```

`npmMinimalAgeGate: 0` — yarn 4.18 quarantines packages whose publish-time
metadata the private registry doesn't serve; the gate is a supply-chain
nicety we can't satisfy against a private registry.

### Storage adapters are composition

A daemon with a non-sqlite storage is a derived image: `FROM` the base and
`yarn add` the adapter — the same `node_modules` the daemon dynamic-imports at
runtime (`--storage <kind>`, [CLI](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/cli)). A private npm registry needs a token
for `yarn add` — pass it as a **BuildKit secret** (never an `ARG`/`ENV`: that
lands in the image layers and `docker history`):

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
FROM ghcr.io/schedjs/sched-daemon:0.11.0
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=registry_token \
    printf 'nodeLinker: node-modules\nnpmMinimalAgeGate: 0\nnpmRegistryServer: "https://registry.npmjs.org"\nnpmAlwaysAuth: true\nnpmAuthToken: "%s"\n' "$(cat /run/secrets/registry_token)" > .yarnrc.yml \
 && CI=1 yarn add @schedjs/storage-mongo@0.5.0 \
 && rm -f .yarnrc.yml
```

```bash
# build it — the token enters via the secret mount, not a build arg
docker build --secret id=registry_token,env=NPM_REGISTRY_TOKEN -t schedd-mongo .
```

`npmMinimalAgeGate: 0` is required against a private registry (yarn 4.18 quarantines
packages whose publish-time metadata the private registry doesn't serve), and
**pin the adapter version explicitly** — an unpinned `yarn add @schedjs/storage-mongo`
can silently resolve an older version (age-gate window), and an adapter without
`createStorage(env)` breaks `--storage mongo` at runtime (books T2 finding
2026-08-22). Pin: `yarn add @schedjs/storage-mongo@0.5.0`.

```bash
# run it — connstring only in env, never in arguments
docker run --rm -e MONGO_URL=mongodb://user:pass@db.internal:27017/sched \
  schedd-mongo --tasks /app/tasks.json --storage mongo
```

Same pattern for `@schedjs/storage-mysql` (`MYSQL_URL`) and
`@schedjs/storage-postgres` (`PG_URL`). A **custom** adapter is an npm package
(or a path mounted into the image) exporting `createStorage(env): Promise<Storage>`
([BYO contract](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/storage/custom)):

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/schedjs/sched-daemon:0.11.0
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=registry_token \
    printf '…registry block (see above)…' > .yarnrc.yml \
 && CI=1 yarn add my-org/sched-storage-redis \
 && rm -f .yarnrc.yml
```

```bash
docker run --rm schedd-mongo --tasks /app/tasks.json --storage my-org/sched-storage-redis
```

If the adapter package is missing from the image, the daemon fails fast with
the exact fix (`RUN yarn add @schedjs/storage-mongo`).

> **Windows (git-bash) operators**: docker run with POSIX-style container paths
> mangles `/app/…` and `/data/…` into `C:/Program Files/Git/…` (→ `unable to open database file`). Prefix the command with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` (or use
> PowerShell / cmd).

## Docker stack (dev)

`docker-compose.dev.yml` at the repo root runs two services:

| Service  | Image                                                              | Ports       | Notes                                                                                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `daemon` | built from `apps/daemon/Dockerfile` (npm-based, `--storage` ready) | 8080        | `--admin-host 0.0.0.0`, `SCHED_ADMIN_KEY=dev-key`, healthcheck with Bearer, SQLite in a volume |
| `shell`  | built from `packages/ui/Dockerfile.serve`                          | 8095 → 8081 | `sched-ui serve`: static UI + proxies `/api` → daemon                                          |

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build
```

Web UI: <http://127.0.0.1:8095>{rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} (shell) · Admin API: <http://127.0.0.1:8080>{rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} (daemon).

## Security model

Auth lives **at the boundaries** — a private network is not authorization:

- **Admin API / UI** — `SCHED_ADMIN_KEY` (Bearer). In production the daemon binds
  `127.0.0.1`/private network, and a reverse proxy (traefik) terminates TLS.
- **Docker runner** — image allowlist (exact + `prefix*`, fail-fast before spawn) and a
  read-only docker-socket proxy (`POST=0`) instead of a raw socket.
- **HTTP runner** — outbound `x-sched-api-key` per task (see
  [HTTP runner](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runners/http)).

## Production deployment (VDS)

Recommended layout behind traefik:

```text
traefik ── basicAuth / forwardAuth ──▶ shell (static UI) + /api
                                         │
daemon ── listens 127.0.0.1 / private ──┘  (SCHED_ADMIN_KEY = second layer)
docker runner ──▶ docker-socket proxy (tecnativa, POST=0) + image allowlist
```

- Terminate TLS at traefik; protect the shell + `/api` with basicAuth (or forwardAuth),
  `SCHED_ADMIN_KEY` adds a second layer.
- The daemon never listens on a public interface.
- Deployment artifacts go through the standard admin flow (Portainer, traefik labels).

## Status alerts

sched can push a notification when a run reaches a **terminal state** — failed by
(default) — or when a **schedule slot fired late** (missed-slot, see below). The
channel is a single **universal outbound webhook** (HTTP `POST` + JSON): the
de-facto standard every external world speaks — Slack / Discord / Teams / Telegram /
ntfy / PagerDuty are all POSTs with different JSON, so one endpoint covers them all.
This is the platform-level signal *that* something finished (and how); content
emails and artifact generation stay with the runner
([who generates what](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runs#artifacts-who-generates-what)).

Configure it two ways — the daemon accepts an `alerts` option in its
`createDaemon` options, **or** (binary workflow, no code) a top-level `alerts`
block in `tasks.json` (`schedd --tasks tasks.json` picks it up like it picks up
`runners`). A programmatic `alerts` option overrides the file block:

```ts
createDaemon({
  tasksPath: 'tasks.json',
  dbPath: 'sched.db',
  alerts: {
    on: ['failed'],   // default — alert on failures only (also: 'succeeded', 'cancelled')
    onMissed: true,   // default — alert on late schedule slots too; set false to silence
    onSyncFailed: true, // default — alert when the tasks.json sync fails (see below); set false to silence
    webhook: {
      url: 'https://hooks.example.com/sched',
      secret: 'whsec_…',              // optional — enables HMAC signature (see below)
      headers: { 'X-Ops-Token': '…' }, // optional — extra headers for your service
      timeoutMs: 10_000,               // optional — per-attempt timeout, default 10s
    },
    tasks: {                          // optional — per-task routing overrides
      'generate-thumbnail': { on: [] },      // silence a cosmetic task
      'sync-payments': { webhook: { url: 'https://hooks.example.com/pagerduty' } }, // different channel
    },
  },
  missedSlotGraceMs: 120_000, // optional — how late a dispatch must be to count as missed (default 2 min)
});
```

**Sync health — `sync.failed`.** The daemon re-reads `tasks.json` on the sync
interval and reconciles. When that sync fails (storage unreachable — a dead
mongo pool means **nothing** schedules, so a `run.failed` alert could never
fire; or a broken file), the daemon POSTs `sync.failed` to the webhook. Payload:

```json
{ "version": 1, "event": "sync.failed", "error": "…", "consecutiveFailures": 1 }
```

Only the **first failure of a streak** fires (dedupe) — a storage that stays
down for a day does not spam one alert per 60s sync tick. When a sync succeeds,
the streak resets and the next incident alerts again.

**Per-task routing.** The root `alerts` block is the channel + defaults; a task can
override its own routing with a task-level `alerts` block in `tasks.json` (or the
`tasks` map above for the programmatic path) — field-wise merge, **task wins,
arrays replace**:

```json
{
  "tasks": [
    { "name": "generate-thumbnail", "runner": "internal", "alerts": { "on": [] } },
    { "name": "sync-payments", "runner": "http", "alerts": { "webhook": { "url": "https://hooks.example.com/pagerduty" } } }
  ],
  "alerts": {
    "on": ["failed"],
    "onMissed": true,
    "webhook": { "url": "https://hooks.example.com/sched", "secret": "whsec_…" }
  }
}
```

- `generate-thumbnail` (`on: []`) stays silent on failure — the root `on` does not
  apply to it. A task **without** an `alerts` block keeps the root defaults.
- `sync-payments` keeps the root `on`/`onMissed` but routes to **its own webhook** —
  the multi-channel escape hatch for criticality ≠ channel.
- Malformed task `alerts` fails at load (see [Tasks → Per-task alert routing](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/tasks#per-task-alert-routing)).

Instead of SQLite you can hand the daemon any storage adapter (see
[Storage](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/storage)) — pass `storage` and omit `dbPath`:

```ts
const storage = await createMysqlStorage(pool); // or postgres / mongo / custom
createDaemon({ tasksPath: 'tasks.json', storage, alerts: { … } });
```

At the **binary** level the same choice is `--storage` (see
[CLI → Storage selection](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/cli#storage-selection-storage)) — the daemon
builds the storage from the connstring env, no code.

```ts
const storage = await createMysqlStorage(pool); // or postgres / mongo / custom
createDaemon({ tasksPath: 'tasks.json', storage, alerts: { … } });
```

### Payload

Every POST carries a JSON body with a `version` (starts at 1 — bump-proof your
consumer against evolution) and an `event` discriminator.

Terminal run states — event is `run.<status>` (`run.failed` / `run.succeeded` /
`run.cancelled`):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "event": "run.failed",
  "task": { "name": "publish-video", "runner": "http" },
  "run": {
    "id": "9f1c…",
    "status": "failed",
    "attempt": 3,
    "error": "connection refused",
    "startedAt": "2026-08-19T09:00:00.000Z",
    "finishedAt": "2026-08-19T09:00:01.000Z"
  }
}
```

Missed slot — a schedule dispatched more than the grace window after its slot
(downtime catch-up, wedged lock):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "event": "missed-slot",
  "task": { "name": "publish-video", "runner": "http" },
  "schedule": { "id": "publish-video#0", "scheduledAt": "2026-08-19T09:00:00.000Z", "delayMs": 32400000 }
}
```

### Signature (HMAC)

When `webhook.secret` is set, sched signs the **exact request body** with
HMAC-SHA256 and sends it as `X-Sched-Signature-256`:

```text
X-Sched-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>
```

Verify on your side (Node):

```ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';

function verify(secret: string, body: string, sig: string | undefined): boolean {
  if (!sig?.startsWith('sha256=')) return false;
  const expected = createHmac('sha256', secret).update(body).digest();
  const received = Buffer.from(sig.slice('sha256='.length), 'hex');
  return received.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(received, expected);
}
```

No `secret` → the POST is unsigned (plain webhook, e.g. into a chat gateway).

### Delivery semantics

- **Bounded retry, never fails the run flow.** Up to **3 attempts** total with
  backoff `5s / 30s`. Network errors, timeouts and `5xx&#x60; are retried; **`4xx` is
  not** (a config error on the sender's side — retrying is pointless, it logs and
  stops). Exhausted → `[alerts]` error log. The run itself is never affected.
- **Persistent failure = the alert point.** A failed run that still has retries
  scheduled does *not* alert — the notification lands only on the final,
  exhausted failure ([Tasks → retry](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/tasks#retry)). Manual `triggerTask` alerts
  immediately and never auto-retries.
- **Missed-slot semantics.** A schedule with run history dispatched more than
  `missedSlotGraceMs` (default 2 min) after its slot fires `missed-slot` —
  engine down at the slot / wedged lock / long queue. The signal is
  cause-agnostic: tune the grace up if your engine legitimately queues runs
  longer than that. Freshly created schedules never fire it — a new schedule's
  first slot is always in the future (past slots are never catch-up-dispatched),
  and the check additionally requires run history (`lastRunAt`), so a
  history-less schedule that is ever dispatched late (e.g. a one-shot with `at`
  in the past) is not reported as a miss either. If the daemon itself is down, detection happens on
  restart — an external uptime monitor covers the gap.
- **Embedded / any engine** — same hooks: `onRunFinal: createAlerts(config).handleFinal`
  plus `onEvent: createAlerts(config).handleEvent` (see
  [Logging → terminal events](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/logging#_2-terminal-events-onrunfinal)).

> CLI/env wiring for alerts is not implemented yet — the surfaces are the
> `createDaemon({ alerts })` option and the `tasks.json` `alerts` block. On
> request it becomes a daemon flag / `SCHED_ALERTS_*` env.

## Storage

SQLite by default (single file, `--db`). MySQL/MariaDB, Postgres and Mongo are
available as storage adapters (shared history across replicas) via `--storage` —
see [CLI → Storage selection](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/cli#storage-selection-storage) and
[Storage](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/storage).


# Security (allowedTools)

Every runner ships a **sandbox** on top of its transport: a deny-by-default-style
allowlist of *tools* a task may use, enforced **before anything spawns** — no
process, container, connection or tool call happens for a non-allowlisted tool.

The model is uniform across runners:

- **Per-task** — `config.allowedTools` declares what *this task* may do. Omitted
  → allow all (the runner ceiling still applies).
- **Runner ceiling** — `options.allowedTools` (daemon: the `runners` block in
  tasks.json) is the *maximum* the runner may ever run. A task whose
  `config.allowedTools` is not a subset of its runner's ceiling **fails at
  load**, before any run.
- **Validation order** — policy first, mechanics second: `allowedTools` shape →
  ceiling subset → runner-specific config (image/command presence, etc.).
  Enforced at load (fail-fast) **and** at every run (a task upserted after
  start is checked too).

## Tool spec format

Uniform pattern language: **exact match or trailing-`*` prefix** (`node`,
`python*`, `alpine:*`, `read_*`). Leading wildcards are not supported. What a
"tool" means is per runner:

| Runner                                                       | Tool identity                     | Example                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| [process](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runners/process) | `argv[0]` (the executable)        | `["node", "python*"]`                          |
| [ssh](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runners/ssh)         | first token of `config.command`   | `["backup.sh", "systemctl*"]`                  |
| [docker](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runners/docker)   | `image@command` (both dimensions) | `["alpine@echo", "registry/*"]`                |
| [mcp](https://schedjs.github.io/schedjs/runners/mcp)         | `server:tool`                     | `["node:read_*", "https://mcp.example.com:*"]` |

### Docker: `image@command`

Docker restricts **two** dimensions — image and explicit entrypoint — in one
spec, separated by `@` (image tags use `:`, so `image:cmd` would be ambiguous):

```json
{ "allowedTools": ["alpine@echo", "alpine", "*@echo"] }
```

- `alpine@echo` — image `alpine`, only when the explicit command is `echo`
- `alpine` (no `@`) — image `alpine`, any command (including the image default)
- `*@echo` — any image, only command `echo`

### MCP: `server:tool`

`server` is the server identity (the URL for http, `command[0]` for stdio), split
on the **last** colon (http servers with ports work:
`https://mcp.example.com:8443:read_data`). A stdio spec without a colon
(`["node"]`) means any tool on that server. Because http URLs carry `:`, a
server-only http spec must be written explicitly as `url:*`. A bare http spec
(`"https://mcp.example.com"` with no `:*`) fails at load with a clear error — it
would otherwise parse as server `https` and silently match nothing.

## Tasks.json

The runner ceiling lives in the top-level `runners` block — policy next to the
desired state:

```json
{
  "runners": {
    "process": { "allowedTools": ["node"] },
    "docker": { "allowedTools": ["alpine@echo"] },
    "ssh": { "allowedTools": ["backup.sh"] },
    "mcp": { "allowedTools": ["node:read_*"] }
  },
  "tasks": [
    {
      "name": "export-captions",
      "runner": "process",
      "schedules": [{ "cron": "0 9 * * *" }],
      "config": {
        "command": ["node", "/opt/scripts/captions.mjs"],
        "allowedTools": ["node"]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Embedded hosts set ceilings directly:
`createDockerRunner({ allowedTools: ['alpine@echo'] })`.

## Security posture

- Omit = allow all (opt-in). A task that declares nothing keeps today's
  behaviour; the ceiling, when set, still applies at run time.
- A non-allowlisted tool never spawns — `failed` with a clear error, not a
  silent skip.
- The allowlist protects the daemon host / remote boxes / tool surface from a
  task whose config came from an untrusted source (agents authoring tasks).
